pointer.quote: The core argument of this work is that the bi-directionality and the two pretraining tasks presented in Section 3.1 account for the majority of the empirical improvements, but we do note that there are several other differences between how BERT and GPT were trained:

evidence.note: fairness/missing_control: For the MNLI improvement over OpenAI GPT, the paper acknowledges other training differences between BERT and GPT, so same data/budget/tuning is not established by the paper-internal comparison.

pointer.quote: • GPT is trained on the BooksCorpus (800M words); BERT is trained on the BooksCorpus (800M words) and Wikipedia (2,500M words).

evidence.note: fairness/missing_control: The MNLI comparison is not controlled for pre-training data: BERT uses BooksCorpus plus Wikipedia, while GPT uses BooksCorpus only.

pointer.quote: • GPT was trained for 1M steps with a batch size of 32,000 words; BERT was trained for 1M steps with a batch size of 128,000 words.

evidence.note: fairness/missing_control: The MNLI comparison is not controlled for pre-training batch/token budget: both are 1M steps, but BERT uses 128,000 words per batch versus GPT's 32,000.

pointer.quote: • GPT used the same learning rate of 5e-5 for all fine-tuning experiments; BERT chooses a task-specific fine-tuning learning rate which performs the best on the development set.

evidence.note: fairness/missing_control: The MNLI comparison is not controlled for fine-tuning learning-rate selection: GPT uses one learning rate, while BERT selects a task-specific rate on the development set.

primary_block.text: Results are presented in Table 1. Both BERT and BERT outperform all systems on all tasks by a substantial margin, obtaining 4.5% and 7.0% respective average accuracy improvement over the prior state of the art. Note that $\mathbf { B E R T _ { B A S E } }$ and OpenAI GPT are nearly identical in terms of model architecture apart from the attention masking. For the largest and most widely reported GLUE task, MNLI, BERT obtains a 4.6% absolute accuracy improvement. On the official GLUE leaderboard<sup>10</sup>, BERT obtains a score of 80.5, compared to OpenAI GPT, which obtains 72.8 as of the date of writing.
